components.note: 阝 (mound, left-side form of 阜 hill) — hills and places: 院, 阳, 陆; 附 is to lean against, to attach.
付 (fù) is an exact sound match; also in 府 fǔ and 符 fú.

example.hanzi: 请看附件里的资料。
example.pinyin: Qǐng kàn fùjiàn lǐ de zīliào.
example.english: Please look at the information in the attachment.
example.fact: 附 means to attach or be near: 附近 (nearby, very common), 附件 (email attachment), 附加 (additional), 附和 (to echo someone). 附中 is a middle school attached to a university.

examples.hanzi: 学校附近有一家书店。
examples.pinyin: Xuéxiào fùjìn yǒu yì jiā shūdiàn.
examples.english: There is a bookstore near the school.

examples.hanzi: 我在邮件后面附上了照片。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zài yóujiàn hòumiàn fùshàng le zhàopiàn.
examples.english: I attached the photos to the email.

components.note: 弓 (bow) — marks bows and bending, as in 张 stretch, 引 draw; 弯 is a curve, like a bent bow.

example.hanzi: 前面的路有一个大弯。
example.pinyin: Qiánmiàn de lù yǒu yí ge dà wān.
example.english: There is a big bend in the road ahead.
example.fact: 弯 means curved or a curve: 拐弯 / 转弯 (to turn a corner), 弯路 (a detour). 绕弯子 means to beat around the bush. Also the measure word for crescent moons: 一弯新月.

examples.hanzi: 你把腰弯下来，看看桌子下面。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ bǎ yāo wān xiàlái, kànkan zhuōzi xiàmiàn.
examples.english: Bend down and look under the table.

examples.hanzi: 往前走，到第二个路口向左拐弯。
examples.pinyin: Wǎng qián zǒu, dào dì èr ge lùkǒu xiàng zuǒ guǎiwān.
examples.english: Go straight and turn left at the second intersection.

components.note: 攵 (tap, strike; 攴) — an action, here to open up; also in 收 gather, 教 teach.
尚 (shàng) gives a loose sound; it also sounds out 常 cháng and 掌 zhǎng.
廾 (two hands) — in 開 two hands lift the bar of a gate; 开 is the simplified shape. Compare 关 (close).

example.hanzi: 她把窗户敞开,让新鲜空气进来。
example.pinyin: tā bǎ chuānghù chǎngkāi, ràng xīnxiān kōngqì jìnlái.
example.english: She opened the window wide to let in fresh air.
example.fact: Boeing's factory in Everett, Washington is the largest building in the world by volume, and its hangar doors open wide enough to roll out multiple wide-body jets side by side. The facility is so large that employees sometimes use bicycles to get from one end of the factory floor to the other.

examples.hanzi: 他把大门敞开，欢迎客人进来。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ dàmén chǎngkāi, huānyíng kèrén jìnlái.
examples.english: He opened the front door wide to welcome the guests in.

examples.hanzi: 她敞开心扉，说出了心里话。
examples.pinyin: Tā chǎngkāi xīnfēi, shuō chū le xīnlǐhuà.
examples.english: She opened her heart and said what was on her mind.

components.note: 囗 (enclosure) — here a mat; oldest form shows a person 大 lying on a mat, "to rely on", later "cause". 因 also sounds out 姻 yīn and 烟 yān.
糸 (silk, simplified 纟) — undyed silk: plain and basic, hence 元素 element and 素食 vegetarian fare.

example.hanzi: 天气是影响农业产量的重要因素。
example.pinyin: tiānqì shì yǐngxiǎng nóngyè chǎnliàng de zhòngyào yīnsù.
example.english: Weather is an important factor affecting agricultural yield.
example.fact: The Rh factor in human blood, the same one behind the '+' or '-' in a blood type, was discovered in 1940 by Karl Landsteiner and Alexander Wiener after they noticed that rabbit antibodies raised against rhesus monkey blood also reacted with most human blood. Identifying this factor was crucial for preventing dangerous immune reactions during blood transfusions and pregnancy.

examples.hanzi: 睡眠不足是造成疲劳的因素之一。
examples.pinyin: Shuìmián bùzú shì zàochéng píláo de yīnsù zhī yī.
examples.english: Lack of sleep is one factor causing fatigue.

examples.hanzi: 价格是我们考虑的主要因素。
examples.pinyin: Jiàgé shì wǒmen kǎolǜ de zhǔyào yīnsù.
examples.english: Price is the main factor we consider.

components.note: 阝 (city, 右耳旁 on the right) — marks places, as in 都 capital, 邮 mail; the gloomy sense of 郁 is a borrowed one.
有 (yǒu) hints at the sound only loosely.
心 (heart) — a gloomy feeling; also in 想 think, 急 anxious.
门 (mén) gives a close sound; 们 men shares it. 闷 reads mēn (stuffy) or mèn (gloomy).

example.hanzi: 考试没考好,他心里很郁闷。
example.pinyin: kǎoshì méi kǎohǎo, tā xīnlǐ hěn yùmèn.
example.english: He did poorly on the exam and felt very gloomy.
example.fact: Seasonal Affective Disorder is a form of depression linked to reduced sunlight exposure, and it is markedly more common in far-northern regions like Scandinavia and Alaska during the darkest winter months. Light therapy, using a bright lamp for a set period each morning, is one of the most common treatments recommended by doctors.

examples.hanzi: 下了一整天雨，我觉得很郁闷。
examples.pinyin: Xià le yì zhěng tiān yǔ, wǒ juéde hěn yùmèn.
examples.english: It rained all day and I feel gloomy.

examples.hanzi: 他一个人待在家里，感到有点郁闷。
examples.pinyin: Tā yí ge rén dāi zài jiā lǐ, gǎndào yǒudiǎn yùmèn.
examples.english: Staying at home alone, he felt a bit down.

components.note: 阝 (mound, 左耳旁 on the left) — hills and heights, as in 院 courtyard, 阳 sunny side, 队 team.
辶 (movement, road) — 辶 marks going and moving, as in 过, 进, 送; 述 is following a story along, to narrate.
术 (shù) — same sound — 述 is shù, like 术 (art, technique).

example.hanzi: 律师向法官陈述了案件的经过。
example.pinyin: lǜshī xiàng fǎguān chénshùle ànjiàn de jīngguò.
example.english: The lawyer stated the details of the case to the judge.
example.fact: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights, adopted by the United Nations General Assembly in 1948, was the first document to formally state a set of fundamental rights believed to belong to all people. It has since been translated into more than 500 languages, making it one of the most translated documents in the world.

examples.hanzi: 请你简单陈述一下事情的经过。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng nǐ jiǎndān chénshù yíxià shìqing de jīngguò.
examples.english: Please briefly state what happened.

examples.hanzi: 他向大家陈述了自己的看法。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiàng dàjiā chénshù le zìjǐ de kànfǎ.
examples.english: He explained his views to everyone.

components.note: 日 (sun) — sunlight falling on everything: universal, common. 普 also sounds out 谱 pǔ.
辶 (walk) — movement and roads, as in 过, 近, 送: a way through.
甬 (yǒng) is a close sound clue for tōng; 甬 also in 痛 tòng, 桶 tǒng and 勇 yǒng.
人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.

example.hanzi: 他只是一个普通人,过着平凡的生活。
example.pinyin: tā zhǐshì yī gè pǔtōngrén, guòzhe píngfán de shēnghuó.
example.english: He is just an ordinary person, living an unremarkable life.
example.fact: The Voyager Golden Record, launched into space in 1977, includes images meant to represent ordinary human life on Earth — people eating, working, and raising families — intended for any intelligent life that might one day encounter the spacecraft. Both Voyager probes have since left the solar system and continue traveling through interstellar space.

examples.hanzi: 普通人也可以做出不平凡的事。
examples.pinyin: Pǔtōngrén yě kěyǐ zuò chū bù píngfán de shì.
examples.english: Ordinary people can also do extraordinary things.

examples.hanzi: 这种手机的价格普通人买得起。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng shǒujī de jiàgé pǔtōngrén mǎi de qǐ.
examples.english: Ordinary people can afford the price of this phone.

components.note: 女 (woman) — traditional reading shows an axe-like weapon 戌 over a woman 女, hence power and authority; compare 姑 and 妈.

example.hanzi: 他在公司很有威信。
example.pinyin: Tā zài gōngsī hěn yǒu wēixìn.
example.english: He has a lot of authority in the company.
example.fact: 威 is about intimidating power: 威力, 威胁 (to threaten), 威风 (imposing), 示威 (to demonstrate). It also shows in names: 威尼斯 (Venice), 威士忌 (whisky).

examples.hanzi: 他很有威信，大家都听他的。
examples.pinyin: Tā hěn yǒu wēixìn, dàjiā dōu tīng tā de.
examples.english: He has great prestige and everyone listens to him.

examples.hanzi: 老板的威严让人有点害怕。
examples.pinyin: Lǎobǎn de wēiyán ràng rén yǒudiǎn hàipà.
examples.english: The boss's authority makes people a bit afraid.

components.note: 戈 (dagger-axe) — marks weapons and striking, as in 战 battle, 武 martial; 戳 is stabbing or poking.

example.hanzi: 别用手指戳我。
example.pinyin: Bié yòng shǒuzhǐ chuō wǒ.
example.english: Don't poke me with your finger.
example.fact: 戳 can be to jab, a seal or a stamp (邮戳 postmark), or fig. to expose: 戳穿谎言 (to expose a lie). Nowadays 戳中 also means "to hit a nerve," as in 戳中泪点.

examples.hanzi: 他用笔戳了一下我的手。
examples.pinyin: Tā yòng bǐ chuō le yíxià wǒ de shǒu.
examples.english: He poked my hand with a pen.

examples.hanzi: 气球被针戳破了。
examples.pinyin: Qìqiú bèi zhēn chuō pò le.
examples.english: The balloon was popped by a needle.

components.note: 巾 (cloth) — the bottom part, as in 布, 帽, 带. 希 is often read as a loosely woven cloth, so 'sparse, rare'; 希望 hope is a later extension.
乂 (crisscross) — Memory aid: crossed threads in an open weave 乂 on cloth 巾 — thin, rare, something you hope for.

example.hanzi: 我希望明天天气好。
example.pinyin: Wǒ xīwàng míngtiān tiānqì hǎo.
example.english: I hope the weather is good tomorrow.
example.fact: 希 is mostly found in 希望 (hope, either noun or verb) and 希腊 (Greece). The "rare" sense survives in 稀 and 希奇. 希望工程 is a well-known charity that helps poor children go to school.

examples.hanzi: 我们都希望你能早点回来。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen dōu xīwàng nǐ néng zǎodiǎn huílái.
examples.english: We all hope you can come back soon.

examples.hanzi: 老师希望大家明天准时到校。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī xīwàng dàjiā míngtiān zhǔnshí dào xiào.
examples.english: The teacher hopes everyone arrives at school on time tomorrow.

components.note: 一 (line) — dictionary reads 不 as a bird flying up toward the sky 一. The meaning 'not' is a borrowing, so the shape does not explain it today.
杯 (bēi) — a character that uses 不 as a loose sound clue (木 + 不). The sound is a hint only: 不 bù vs bēi.
足 (foot) — a kneecap 口 above a foot 止; as the radical ⻊ it marks feet and walking: 跑, 跳, 路, 踢. Also means enough.

example.hanzi: 这份报告的数据明显不足。
example.pinyin: zhè fèn bàogào de shùjù míngxiǎn bùzú.
example.english: The data in this report is clearly insufficient.
example.fact: Scurvy, caused by insufficient vitamin C, devastated sailors on long ocean voyages for centuries, killing more seamen than storms or combat. In 1747, ship's surgeon James Lind ran one of the first controlled clinical trials in history and showed that citrus fruit cured the disease, decades before vitamin C itself was even identified.

examples.hanzi: 我们的时间不足，只能下次再讨论。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen de shíjiān bùzú, zhǐ néng xiàcì zài tǎolùn.
examples.english: We don't have enough time, so we can only discuss it next time.

examples.hanzi: 他的经验还有不足，需要继续学习。
examples.pinyin: Tā de jīngyàn hái yǒu bùzú, xūyào jìxù xuéxí.
examples.english: His experience is still lacking, so he needs to keep learning.

components.note: 女 (woman) — women and family, as in 妈, 她, 姐.
子 (child) — a woman with her child: the picture of something good.
口 (mouth) — sound and speech, as in 吃, 唱, 问.
斤 (jīn, axe) is only a loose clue for tīng; the traditional 聽 had 耳 ear.

example.hanzi: 这首歌的旋律非常好听。
example.pinyin: zhè shǒu gē de xuánlǜ fēicháng hǎotīng.
example.english: The melody of this song is very pleasant to listen to.
example.fact: Humpback whales produce long, complex songs made of repeating phrases that can travel for many kilometers underwater and be picked up by whales far across an ocean basin. Researchers have found that these songs evolve over time and can spread between whale populations almost like a cultural trend.

examples.hanzi: 她的声音很好听。
examples.pinyin: Tā de shēngyīn hěn hǎotīng.
examples.english: Her voice is very pleasant.

examples.hanzi: 这个名字真好听，是谁取的？
examples.pinyin: Zhège míngzi zhēn hǎotīng, shì shéi qǔ de?
examples.english: This name sounds so nice, who picked it?

components.note: 辶 (walk) — movement and roads, as in 过, 近, 送: following the edge. The part 力 stands in for 臱 in the traditional 邊.
土 (earth) — 土 is earth and land, as in 地, 城, 块; 境 is a stretch of land, a border or condition.
竟 (jìng) — same sound — 境 is jìng, like 竟; 竟 also sounds out 镜 jìng.

example.hanzi: 士兵们日夜守卫着边境。
example.pinyin: shìbīngmen rìyè shǒuwèizhe biānjìng.
example.english: The soldiers guard the border day and night.
example.fact: The border between the United States and Canada stretches about 8,891 kilometers, including Alaska, making it the longest international border in the world. Much of it is unguarded by fences, relying instead on periodic monitoring and shared agreements between the two countries.

examples.hanzi: 这条河是两国的边境。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo hé shì liǎng guó de biānjìng.
examples.english: This river is the border between the two countries.

examples.hanzi: 边境附近的小镇很安静。
examples.pinyin: Biānjìng fùjìn de xiǎozhèn hěn ānjìng.
examples.english: The small town near the border is very quiet.

components.note: 巾 (cloth) — a scarf or handkerchief; also in 布 cloth, 帽 hat.
白 (bái) is a loose clue; 怕 pà shares it and sounds exactly like 帕.

example.hanzi: 她用手帕擦了擦眼泪。
example.pinyin: Tā yòng shǒupà cā le cā yǎnlèi.
example.english: She wiped her tears with a handkerchief.
example.fact: 帕 sits in 手帕 (handkerchief) and 头帕 (headscarf). It also stands in for the pascal, the unit of pressure, and for sounds in names such as 帕金森 (Parkinson).

examples.hanzi: 他从口袋里拿出一块手帕。
examples.pinyin: Tā cóng kǒudài lǐ ná chū yí kuài shǒupà.
examples.english: He took a handkerchief out of his pocket.

examples.hanzi: 奶奶头上围着一条旧头帕。
examples.pinyin: Nǎinai tóu shàng wéi zhe yì tiáo jiù tóupà.
examples.english: Grandma wears an old kerchief on her head.

components.note: 贝 (shell, old money) — giving wealth; also in 财 wealth, 买 buy.
易 (yì) is only a loose sound clue for cì.

example.hanzi: 皇帝赐给他一件宝物。
example.pinyin: Huángdì cì gěi tā yí jiàn bǎowù.
example.english: The emperor bestowed a treasure on him.
example.fact: 赐 is a gift from a superior, such as an emperor: 赏赐, 恩赐. Politely, 请多赐教 ("please favor me with your guidance") is a humble stock phrase, and 天赐良机 means a golden opportunity from heaven.

examples.hanzi: 这次机会是老天赐给我的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì jīhuì shì lǎotiān cì gěi wǒ de.
examples.english: This opportunity was given to me by heaven.

examples.hanzi: 请您多多赐教。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng nín duōduō cìjiào.
examples.english: Please give me your guidance.

components.note: 亻 (person) — marks people and their roles, as in 你 you, 们 plural, 信 trust; 仙 is an immortal, a person of the mountains.
山 (mountain) — a person 亻 of the mountains 山: a hermit immortal, as in 神仙.

example.hanzi: 传说山上住着一位神仙。
example.pinyin: Chuánshuō shān shàng zhù zhe yí wèi shénxiān.
example.english: Legend says an immortal lives on the mountain.
example.fact: 仙 refers to immortals in Daoist belief and is often explained as "a person living in the mountains." See 神仙 (gods and immortals), 仙女 (fairy maiden), 成仙 (to become immortal) and 仙人掌 (cactus).

examples.hanzi: 这个故事里有一位美丽的仙女。
examples.pinyin: Zhège gùshi lǐ yǒu yí wèi měilì de xiānnǚ.
examples.english: There is a beautiful fairy in this story.

examples.hanzi: 水仙花在冬天开放。
examples.pinyin: Shuǐxiān huā zài dōngtiān kāifàng.
examples.english: Narcissus flowers bloom in winter.

components.note: 发 (send out, hair) — two characters merged in simplified writing: 發 fā "emit, issue" and 髮 fà "hair" (头发).
纟 (thread, simplified 糸) — silk and cord: 红, 线, 组; 给 is to supply thread, then to give.
合 (hé) is only a loose sound clue; same part in 答 dá, 拾 shí, 恰 qià.

example.hanzi: 老师把成绩单发给了每个学生。
example.pinyin: lǎoshī bǎ chéngjìdān fāgěile měi gè xuésheng.
example.english: The teacher distributed the report cards to every student.
example.fact: Around 1023 CE, the Song dynasty government in China began issuing jiaozi, generally regarded as the world's first government-backed paper currency, after private merchant notes became too widespread to regulate. This innovation predated paper money in Europe by several centuries.

examples.hanzi: 公司每月都会发给员工奖金。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī měi yuè dōu huì fā gěi yuángōng jiǎngjīn.
examples.english: The company gives its employees a bonus every month.

examples.hanzi: 请把这些传单发给路过的人。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ zhèxiē chuándān fā gěi lùguò de rén.
examples.english: Please hand these flyers out to people passing by.

components.note: 疒 (illness, 病字旁) — sickness and healing: 病, 痛, 症; 疗 is to treat illness.
了 (liǎo) stands in for the sound of traditional 療 (liáo), close to liáo.
氵 (water) — water, as in 河, 海, 清: in the old form 灋, water stood for fairness, so law and method.

example.hanzi: 医生建议用新的疗法治疗这种疾病。
example.pinyin: yīshēng jiànyì yòng xīn de liáofǎ zhìliáo zhè zhǒng jíbìng.
example.english: The doctor recommended treating this disease with a new therapy.
example.fact: Penicillin, the first widely used antibiotic therapy, was discovered by accident in 1928 when Alexander Fleming noticed that mold contaminating one of his bacterial cultures was killing the surrounding bacteria. It wasn't mass-produced until the 1940s, just in time to treat wounded soldiers during World War II, and it is credited with saving hundreds of millions of lives since.

examples.hanzi: 这种疗法对背痛很有效。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng liáofǎ duì bèitòng hěn yǒuxiào.
examples.english: This therapy is very effective for back pain.

examples.hanzi: 医生比较了几种不同的疗法。
examples.pinyin: Yīshēng bǐjiào le jǐ zhǒng bùtóng de liáofǎ.
examples.english: The doctor compared several different treatments.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — marks actions done by hand, as in 打, 推, 拿; 掩 is to cover with the hand.
奄 (yǎn) gives the sound: 掩 yǎn, close to 淹 yān and 腌 yān.
巾 (cloth) — marks cloth and coverings, as in 布, 帽, 带; decorating was often done with cloth.
饣 (here from 食 shí) is the sound part: 饰 shì is close.

example.hanzi: 他试图掩饰自己的紧张。
example.pinyin: tā shìtú yǎnshì zìjǐ de jǐnzhāng.
example.english: He tried to conceal his nervousness.
example.fact: Cuttlefish can change both the color and the texture of their skin within a fraction of a second, using specialized cells called chromatophores to conceal themselves from predators or mimic their surroundings. Despite being colorblind, they can match complex backgrounds with startling accuracy.

examples.hanzi: 他用笑容掩饰内心的难过。
examples.pinyin: Tā yòng xiàoróng yǎnshì nèixīn de nánguò.
examples.english: He used a smile to hide his sadness.

examples.hanzi: 她想掩饰自己的错误，但没成功。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎng yǎnshì zìjǐ de cuòwù, dàn méi chénggōng.
examples.english: She tried to cover up her mistake, but she failed.

components.note: 疋 (foot) — the lower right. Dictionary story: an old man walking 疋 with a cane. Early forms show a person looking around, unsure. Treat as a memory aid.
矢 (arrow) — Dictionary reads it as a cane held by an old man; memory aid: an old man leaning on a stick, unsure which way — doubt, 怀疑.
门 (mén, gate) is a close sound clue for wèn; the picture is asking at a gate, as in 闻 wén.
口 (mouth) — speaking, as in 吃, 唱, 叫: asking is a mouth action.

example.hanzi: 这个问题至今仍是一个疑问。
example.pinyin: zhège wèntí zhìjīn réng shì yī gè yíwèn.
example.english: This question remains a doubt to this day.
example.fact: The philosopher Karl Popper argued that genuine scientific claims must be falsifiable — capable of being proven wrong through observation or experiment. This principle of built-in doubt became one of the central standards used to distinguish science from pseudoscience throughout the twentieth century.

examples.hanzi: 大家对这个计划还有什么疑问吗？
examples.pinyin: Dàjiā duì zhège jìhuà hái yǒu shénme yíwèn ma?
examples.english: Does anyone still have questions about this plan?

examples.hanzi: 他的话毫无疑问是真的。
examples.pinyin: Tā de huà háo wú yíwèn shì zhēn de.
examples.english: What he said is undoubtedly true.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — blocking with the hand; also in 推 push, 打 hit.
当 (dāng) gives the sound, with a different tone; 档 dàng shares it.
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做.
主 (zhǔ) is a close sound clue for zhù; also in 注 zhù and 柱 zhù, and 主 means master (a person who stays).

example.hanzi: 一棵大树挡住了我们的视线。
example.pinyin: yī kē dà shù dǎngzhùle wǒmen de shìxiàn.
example.english: A big tree blocked our view.
example.fact: Beaver dams can grow large enough to block entire rivers and reshape local ecosystems; the largest known beaver dam, in Alberta, Canada, stretches over 850 meters and is visible in satellite imagery. Beavers build these structures instinctively to create the still water they need for safety and food storage.

examples.hanzi: 别挡住我，我要过去。
examples.pinyin: Bié dǎngzhù wǒ, wǒ yào guòqù.
examples.english: Don't block me, I need to get through.

examples.hanzi: 大雪挡住了回家的路。
examples.pinyin: Dàxuě dǎngzhù le huíjiā de lù.
examples.english: The heavy snow blocked the road home.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — marks actions done by hand, as in 打, 拉, 提; 操 is to handle or drill.
喿 (zào) hints at the sound: 操 cāo is close to 澡 zǎo and 燥 zào.
心 (heart) — a picture of a heart. Written 忄 on the left (快, 怕) and 心 at the bottom (想, 思, 忘); it marks feelings and thoughts.

example.hanzi: 别再为这点小事操心了。
example.pinyin: bié zài wèi zhè diǎn xiǎoshì cāoxīn le.
example.english: Don't worry about such a small matter anymore.
example.fact: Chronic worry triggers the adrenal glands to release cortisol, a stress hormone that, in short bursts, sharpens focus but that, over long periods, can suppress immune function and disrupt sleep. Studies on prolonged stress have linked it to slower wound healing and greater susceptibility to common illnesses.

examples.hanzi: 妈妈总是为孩子操心。
examples.pinyin: Māma zǒngshì wèi háizi cāoxīn.
examples.english: Mom is always worrying about her kids.

examples.hanzi: 你别操心了，我自己能处理。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ bié cāoxīn le, wǒ zìjǐ néng chǔlǐ.
examples.english: Don't worry, I can handle it myself.

components.note: 丬 (bed) — near sound — 壮 is zhuàng; 丬 also sounds out 状 zhuàng and 装 zhuāng.
士 (scholar, man) — 士 is a man, as in 战士; 壮 is a strong man.

example.hanzi: 他长得很壮，力气很大。
example.pinyin: Tā zhǎng de hěn zhuàng, lìqi hěn dà.
example.english: He is sturdily built and very strong.
example.fact: 壮 means strong or magnificent: 强壮, 壮观 (spectacular), 壮士 (a brave warrior), 壮胆 (to boost one's courage). 壮族 is the Zhuang people, China's largest ethnic minority.

examples.hanzi: 这头牛长得又高又壮，力气很大。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tóu niú zhǎng de yòu gāo yòu zhuàng, lìqi hěn dà.
examples.english: This ox is tall and sturdy.

examples.hanzi: 他每天锻炼，身体越来越强壮。
examples.pinyin: Tā měitiān duànliàn, shēntǐ yuè lái yuè qiángzhuàng.
examples.english: He exercises every day and is getting stronger and stronger.

components.note: 纟 (silk thread, from 糸) — marks thread and ties, as in 线, 红, 约; 维 is a rope that holds things together.
隹 (zhuī, short-tailed bird) is only a loose sound clue for wéi, as in 推 tuī and 谁 shéi.
扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 打, 拿, 抱: guarding with the hands.
户 (hù, door) gives the exact sound; 户 means door or household.

example.hanzi: 政府有责任维护社会秩序。
example.pinyin: zhèngfǔ yǒu zérèn wéihù shèhuì zhìxù.
example.english: The government has a responsibility to safeguard social order.
example.fact: The Golden Gate Bridge employs a dedicated crew of ironworkers and painters who continuously maintain its signature orange coat, because salty sea air from the Bay corrodes the steel far faster than in a typical environment. The maintenance cycle never truly ends — by the time one end of the bridge is finished, the other end already needs attention again.

examples.hanzi: 我们要维护公共环境的整洁。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào wéihù gōnggòng huánjìng de zhěngjié.
examples.english: We should keep the public environment tidy.

examples.hanzi: 工程师定期维护这些机器。
examples.pinyin: Gōngchéngshī dìngqī wéihù zhèxiē jīqì.
examples.english: Engineers maintain these machines regularly.

components.note: 亻 (person) — a person's precedent or example; also in 他 he, 做 do.
列 (liè) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 烈 liè and 裂 liè.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.hanzi: 老师举了一个简单的例子来解释这个概念。
example.pinyin: lǎoshī jǔle yī gè jiǎndān de lìzi lái jiěshì zhège gàiniàn.
example.english: The teacher gave a simple example to explain the concept.
example.fact: The fruit fly Drosophila melanogaster has served as a classic example organism in genetics for over a century, because it breeds quickly, has a short lifespan, and shares many genes with humans. Research using this simple insect has contributed to at least six Nobel Prizes in Physiology or Medicine.

examples.hanzi: 请举个例子说明一下。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng jǔ ge lìzi shuōmíng yíxià.
examples.english: Please give an example to explain.

examples.hanzi: 这是一个成功的例子。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì yí ge chénggōng de lìzi.
examples.english: This is a successful example.

components.note: 犬 (dog) — a sacrifice was offered with a dog, hence 献 is to present or offer; the left side is a simplified stand-in.
纟 (thread, simplified 糸) — silk and cord: 红, 线, 组; 给 is to supply thread, then to give.
合 (hé) is only a loose sound clue; same part in 答 dá, 拾 shí, 恰 qià.

example.hanzi: 这首歌是献给他母亲的。
example.pinyin: zhè shǒu gē shì xiàngěi tā mǔqīn de.
example.english: This song is dedicated to his mother.
example.fact: The Taj Mahal, one of the most recognized buildings in the world, was commissioned by the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan as a mausoleum dedicated to his wife, Mumtaz Mahal, who died during childbirth in 1631. Construction took roughly two decades and reportedly involved thousands of craftsmen and artisans brought in from across the empire.

examples.hanzi: 他把毕业作品献给了老师。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ bìyè zuòpǐn xiàn gěi le lǎoshī.
examples.english: He dedicated his graduation work to his teacher.

examples.hanzi: 学生们把鲜花献给了老人。
examples.pinyin: Xuéshengmen bǎ xiānhuā xiàn gěi le lǎorén.
examples.english: The students presented flowers to the elderly people.

components.note: 纟 (thread, simplified 糸) — silk and cord words: 红 red, 给 give, 线 line; a thread has an end, which fits 终 end.
冬 (dōng) rhymes with 终 zhōng, and 冬 originally meant the end (of the year) too — so it helps sound and sense.
灬 (fire) — heat and burning, as in 热 hot, 照 shine, 黑 black; a dot is a small spot like a spark.
占 (zhàn) is a loose sound clue for diǎn; 占 also sounds out 站 zhàn and 粘 zhān.

example.hanzi: 运动员们终于到达了终点。
example.pinyin: yùndòngyuánmen zhōngyú dàodále zhōngdiǎn.
example.english: The athletes finally reached the finish line.
example.fact: The modern marathon's standard distance, 42.195 kilometers, was fixed based on the course used at the 1908 London Olympics, which ran from Windsor Castle to White City Stadium. Earlier Olympic marathons had varied in length, and this particular route just happened to become the permanent standard adopted worldwide.

examples.hanzi: 马拉松的终点在公园门口。
examples.pinyin: Mǎlāsōng de zhōngdiǎn zài gōngyuán ménkǒu.
examples.english: The marathon finish line is at the park entrance.

examples.hanzi: 这趟列车的终点是上海。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tàng lièchē de zhōngdiǎn shì Shànghǎi.
examples.english: The terminus of this train is Shanghai.

components.note: 亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 作. 做 is a later variant of 作 zuò (to do), sharing its meaning and sound.
故 (gù) is only a loose sound hint.
成 (chéng) is a sound clue for 城 chéng, 诚 chéng and 盛 chéng: the same sound.

example.hanzi: 她把这块布做成了一条裙子。
example.pinyin: tā bǎ zhè kuài bù zuòchéngle yī tiáo qúnzi.
example.english: She made this piece of cloth into a skirt.
example.fact: Ordinary glass is made by heating common sand, primarily silica, to temperatures above 1,700 degrees Celsius until it melts into a liquid that can be shaped and cooled into a solid, transparent material. Ancient Mesopotamian and Egyptian artisans were making glass objects as early as 3,500 years ago, long before industrial furnaces existed.

examples.hanzi: 我们想把旧房子做成一家咖啡馆。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xiǎng bǎ jiù fángzi zuòchéng yì jiā kāfēiguǎn.
examples.english: We want to turn the old house into a café.

examples.hanzi: 这笔生意终于做成了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bǐ shēngyi zhōngyú zuòchéng le.
examples.english: This deal was finally closed.

components.note: 木 (wood, tree) — 条 was a long slender twig, so branch, strip, and then the measure word for long things; 木 as in 树, 板.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.hanzi: 他在桌上留了一张条子。
example.pinyin: tā zài zhuō shàng liúle yī zhāng tiáozi.
example.english: He left a note on the table.
example.fact: The Rosetta Stone, discovered in 1799, carries the same royal decree written in three different scripts — hieroglyphic, Demotic, and Ancient Greek. Because the Greek text could already be read, scholars used the stone to finally decipher Egyptian hieroglyphics, unlocking centuries of previously unreadable inscriptions.

examples.hanzi: 他穿着一件条子衬衫。
examples.pinyin: Tā chuānzhe yí jiàn tiáozi chènshān.
examples.english: He is wearing a striped shirt.

examples.hanzi: 请在这张条子上写下你的电话号码。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng zài zhè zhāng tiáozi shàng xiěxià nǐ de diànhuà hàomǎ.
examples.english: Please write your phone number on this slip of paper.

components.note: 纟 (silk, simplified 糸) — taking in thread; also in 红 red, 级 level.
内 (nèi) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 钠 nà (sodium).
米 (rice, grain) — pure unmixed grain, hence essence; also in 粉 powder, 粮 grain.
卒 (zú) is a loose clue; it starts the cuì series 翠 cuì, 悴 cuì and 瘁 cuì.

example.hanzi: 这部电影讲述了二战期间纳粹的暴行。
example.pinyin: zhè bù diànyǐng jiǎngshùle èrzhàn qījiān Nàcuì de bàoxíng.
example.english: This film tells of the Nazis' atrocities during World War II.
example.fact: The Nuremberg Trials, held from 1945 to 1946, were the first international tribunals to prosecute individuals for crimes against humanity, establishing the legal precedent that following orders is not a defense for atrocities. The trials introduced legal concepts still used in international courts today, including genocide as a distinct, prosecutable crime.

examples.hanzi: 博物馆里展出了纳粹时期的历史资料。
examples.pinyin: Bówùguǎn lǐ zhǎnchū le Nàcuì shíqī de lìshǐ zīliào.
examples.english: The museum displays historical materials from the Nazi era.

examples.hanzi: 他读了一本关于纳粹历史的书。
examples.pinyin: Tā dú le yì běn guānyú Nàcuì lìshǐ de shū.
examples.english: He read a book about the history of the Nazis.

components.note: 雨 (rain) — marks weather and moisture, as in 雪 snow, 雷 thunder, 露 dew; fog is water hanging in the air.
务 (wù) — same sound: 雾 wù. 务 also appears in 误 wù.

example.hanzi: 今天早上有大雾。
example.pinyin: Jīntiān zǎoshang yǒu dà wù.
example.english: There was thick fog this morning.
example.fact: 雾 is fog: 大雾, 云雾, 喷雾 (spray). 雾霾 is smog (fog plus haze), a news staple in northern China. The idiom 雾里看花 (looking at flowers through fog) describes seeing something unclearly.

examples.hanzi: 山里的雾很大，什么都看不见。
examples.pinyin: Shān lǐ de wù hěn dà, shénme dōu kàn bu jiàn.
examples.english: The fog in the mountains is thick and you cannot see anything.

examples.hanzi: 因为大雾，飞机晚点了。
examples.pinyin: Yīnwèi dàwù, fēijī wǎndiǎn le.
examples.english: The flight was delayed because of heavy fog.

meanings: Asia (abbr. for 亞細亞洲|亚细亚洲[Ya4 xi4 ya4 Zhou1])

components.note: 亚 (yà) — Asia; as a part it sounds out 哑 yǎ and 娅 yà.
氵 (water) — 氵 is water, as in 河, 海; 洲 is land surrounded by water.
州 (zhōu) — same sound — 洲 is zhōu, like 州; continents like 亚洲 are 洲.

example.hanzi: 中国是亚洲最大的国家之一。
example.pinyin: Zhōngguó shì Yàzhōu zuìdà de guójiā zhī yī.
example.english: China is one of the largest countries in Asia.
example.fact: Asia is Earth's largest continent by both area and population, covering roughly 30 percent of the planet's total land area and home to more than 4.7 billion people. It contains both the highest point on Earth, Mount Everest, and the lowest exposed land point, the shore of the Dead Sea.

examples.hanzi: 亚洲有很多不同的文化。
examples.pinyin: Yàzhōu yǒu hěn duō bùtóng de wénhuà.
examples.english: Asia has many different cultures.

examples.hanzi: 我打算明年去亚洲旅行。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ dǎsuàn míngnián qù Yàzhōu lǚxíng.
examples.english: I plan to travel to Asia next year.

components.note: 尸 (body) — a body being butchered; also in 层 layer, 屋 room.
者 (zhě) is only a loose sound clue; 堵 dǔ and 赌 dǔ also use it.
乂 (to cut, crisscross) — old for mowing or cutting. Dictionary story: someone cut down 乂 and buried in a wooden coffin 木, a vivid memory aid.
木 (tree, wood) — the bottom. In 杀 it is a leftover of the old 殺 form rather than meaning wood; 殺 also had 殳 (weapon in hand).

example.hanzi: 历史书记录了那场可怕的屠杀。
example.pinyin: lìshǐshū jìlùle nà chǎng kěpà de túshā.
example.english: The history book records that terrible massacre.
example.fact: The passenger pigeon was once the most abundant bird in North America, with flocks so vast they could darken the sky for hours as they passed overhead. Relentless commercial hunting through the 1800s drove the species from billions of individuals to complete extinction by 1914, one of the fastest documented collapses of an animal population in history.

examples.hanzi: 动物保护组织反对屠杀野生动物。
examples.pinyin: Dòngwù bǎohù zǔzhī fǎnduì túshā yěshēng dòngwù.
examples.english: Animal protection groups oppose the slaughter of wild animals.

examples.hanzi: 老师给我们讲了一段关于屠杀的历史教训。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī gěi wǒmen jiǎng le yí duàn guānyú túshā de lìshǐ jiàoxùn.
examples.english: The teacher told us about a historical lesson on massacres.

meanings: strike (i.e. angle of inclination in geology)

components.note: 走 (walk, run) — a person with swinging arms above a foot 止. As a radical it marks movement: 起, 越, 超, 趣.
向 (toward) — a window 口 in a wall facing a direction, hence toward. It also gives its sound to 响 xiǎng and 饷 xiǎng.

example.hanzi: 专家们讨论了经济未来的走向。
example.pinyin: zhuānjiāmen tǎolùnle jīngjì wèilái de zǒuxiàng.
example.english: Experts discussed the future trend of the economy.
example.fact: In geology, 'strike' describes the compass direction along which a tilted rock layer intersects a horizontal plane, a measurement geologists use to map underground formations and fault lines. Understanding the strike and dip of rock layers along California's San Andreas Fault has been essential to predicting earthquake risk in the region.

examples.hanzi: 这条河的走向是从北到南。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo hé de zǒuxiàng shì cóng běi dào nán.
examples.english: This river runs from north to south.

examples.hanzi: 这部电影的故事走向很出人意料。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng de gùshi zǒuxiàng hěn chū rén yìliào.
examples.english: The story's direction in this movie was quite unexpected.

components.note: 里 (village, land) — in 野 it means land: open country beyond the village, wild, as in 野兽.
予 (yǔ) hints at the sound: 野 yě is close to 预 yù and 序 xù.
虫 (insect, creature) — marks small creatures, as in 蛇 snake, 蚊 mosquito; in 蛮 it is part of an old, derogatory label for outsiders.

example.hanzi: 这种野蛮的行为让人无法接受。
example.pinyin: zhè zhǒng yěmán de xíngwéi ràng rén wúfǎ jiēshòu.
example.english: This kind of barbarous behavior is unacceptable.
example.fact: Primatologist Jane Goodall was the first researcher to document chimpanzees engaging in coordinated, sustained violence between rival troops, a finding that startled scientists who had assumed only humans waged organized conflict. Her observations at Gombe Stream National Park in Tanzania in the 1970s reshaped how biologists think about the origins of group aggression.

examples.hanzi: 古代的人用野蛮的方式解决问题。
examples.pinyin: Gǔdài de rén yòng yěmán de fāngshì jiějué wèntí.
examples.english: People in ancient times solved problems in savage ways.

examples.hanzi: 别这么野蛮，好好说话。
examples.pinyin: Bié zhème yěmán, hǎohāo shuōhuà.
examples.english: Don't be so uncivilized, speak properly.

components.note: 会 (meet, can) — simplified from 會, a lid on a container: bringing things together; hence meeting, then "can" (huì).
讠 (speech, simplified 言) — talking and language: 说 say, 请 ask, 话 speech; 议 is to discuss.
义 (yì) sounds exactly like 议; same part in 仪 yí and 蚁 yǐ.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 安, 字: a room under the roof.
至 (zhì, arrive) is a loose sound clue for shì; it fits the meaning: where one arrives inside the house.

example.hanzi: 我们在会议室里讨论了新方案。
example.pinyin: wǒmen zài huìyìshì lǐ tǎolùnle xīn fāng'àn.
example.english: We discussed the new plan in the meeting room.
example.fact: The United Nations Security Council Chamber in New York features a large mural donated by Norway depicting a phoenix rising from ashes, symbolizing a world rebuilding itself after the devastation of World War II. The room has hosted the council's meetings since the UN headquarters opened in 1952.

examples.hanzi: 会议室在二楼，请跟我来。
examples.pinyin: Huìyìshì zài èr lóu, qǐng gēn wǒ lái.
examples.english: The meeting room is on the second floor, please follow me.

examples.hanzi: 这间会议室可以坐二十个人。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiān huìyìshì kěyǐ zuò èrshí ge rén.
examples.english: This meeting room can seat twenty people.

components.note: 扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 抱; 提 is to lift or carry in the hand.
是 (shì) is a loose sound hint; the same part is in 题 tí and 堤 dī.
口 (mouth) — calling out; 夕 (evening) beside it: in the dark you cannot be seen, so you call your name.

example.hanzi: 她被提名为最佳女演员。
example.pinyin: tā bèi tímíng wéi zuìjiā nǚ yǎnyuán.
example.english: She was nominated for best actress.
example.fact: Nobel Prize nominations are kept confidential for 50 years before being released to the public in the Nobel archive, meaning nominees and nominators from the mid-twentieth century are only now becoming fully known. Some of the disclosed archives have revealed surprising near-misses, including scientists later found to have been nominated many times without ever winning.

examples.hanzi: 这部电影被提名为最佳影片。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng bèi tímíng wéi zuìjiā yǐngpiàn.
examples.english: This film was nominated for best picture.

examples.hanzi: 大家提名他当班长。
examples.pinyin: Dàjiā tímíng tā dāng bānzhǎng.
examples.english: Everyone nominated him as class monitor.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢.
周 (zhōu) is a loose sound clue for diào/tiáo; 周 also in 凋 diāo.
忄 (heart) — feelings, as in 快 happy, 怕 afraid, 忙 busy.
青 (qīng) is a close sound clue for qíng; the series 清 qīng, 请 qǐng, 晴 qíng, 精 jīng.

example.hanzi: 他喜欢和陌生人调情。
example.pinyin: tā xǐhuan hé mòshēngrén tiáoqíng.
example.english: He likes to flirt with strangers.
example.fact: Peacocks display their iridescent tail feathers in elaborate courtship dances, and the number and symmetry of eyespots directly influence which males females choose to mate with. Charles Darwin used this kind of showy, seemingly impractical display as a key example when developing his theory of sexual selection.

examples.hanzi: 他在酒吧里和一位女士调情。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài jiǔbā lǐ hé yí wèi nǚshì tiáoqíng.
examples.english: He flirted with a woman at the bar.

examples.hanzi: 别在工作场合调情，这样不合适。
examples.pinyin: Bié zài gōngzuò chǎnghé tiáoqíng, zhèyàng bù héshì.
examples.english: Don't flirt at work, it isn't appropriate.

components.note: 艹 (grass) — plants; also in 花 flower, 草 grass.
重 (zhòng) is only a loose clue; 懂 dǒng (to understand) shares 董 and sounds the same.
彐 (hand-like part) — 事 is usually explained as a hand holding a tool or tally, 'handling business' — a hedged reading, not certain.
史 (history, scribe) — shares an ancient root with 事: a hand holding a recording tool. Both are about handling official 'matters'.
会 (meet, can) — simplified from 會, a lid on a container: bringing things together; hence meeting, then "can" (huì).

example.hanzi: 董事会将在下周开会讨论预算。
example.pinyin: dǒngshìhuì jiāng zài xià zhōu kāihuì tǎolùn yùsuàn.
example.english: The board of directors will meet next week to discuss the budget.
example.fact: The Dutch East India Company, founded in 1602, is widely considered the first corporation to be run by a formal board of directors and to issue shares that could be freely traded on an open exchange. Its structure laid much of the groundwork for how modern publicly traded companies are organized.

examples.hanzi: 董事会通过了新的计划。
examples.pinyin: Dǒngshìhuì tōngguò le xīn de jìhuà.
examples.english: The board of directors approved the new plan.

examples.hanzi: 他是公司董事会的成员。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì gōngsī dǒngshìhuì de chéngyuán.
examples.english: He is a member of the company's board of directors.

components.note: 身 (body) — the body ducking away; also in 躺 lie down, 躬.
朵 (duǒ) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 垛 duò.
辶 (movement, road) — 辶 marks going and moving, as in 过, 进, 逃; 避 is stepping aside.
辟 (bì) — same sound — 避 is bì, like 辟; 辟 also sounds out 壁 bì and 臂 bì.

example.hanzi: 小动物们躲避着凶猛的老鹰。
example.pinyin: xiǎo dòngwùmen duǒbìzhe xiōngměng de lǎoyīng.
example.english: The little animals evaded the fierce eagle.
example.fact: The octopus can instantly change both the color and the texture of its skin to evade predators, using muscle-controlled papillae to mimic rocks, coral, or sand within moments. Neuroscientists still don't fully understand how the octopus's decentralized nervous system coordinates such precise camouflage across its entire body.

examples.hanzi: 下雨了，我们先躲避一下吧。
examples.pinyin: Xiàyǔ le, wǒmen xiān duǒbì yíxià ba.
examples.english: It's raining, so let's take shelter first.

examples.hanzi: 他想躲避责任，但没有用。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎng duǒbì zérèn, dàn méiyǒu yòng.
examples.english: He tried to dodge responsibility, but it was no use.

components.note: 土 (earth) — a green shoot pushing up from the ground: growth, birth, life. 生 also sounds out 性 xìng, 姓 xìng and 星 xīng.
歹 (bad bone) — death and decay, as in 残 remnant, 烈 fierce, 殊 special.
匕 (person) — a person beside bones: death.

example.hanzi: 医生在手术室里面对生死的考验。
example.pinyin: yīshēng zài shǒushùshì lǐ miànduì shēngsǐ de kǎoyàn.
example.english: The doctor faced a test of life or death in the operating room.
example.fact: Telomeres, the protective caps at the ends of chromosomes, shorten slightly every time a cell divides, and once they grow too short, the cell can no longer replicate. This process is closely linked to aging, and the scientists who discovered how telomeres are maintained by the enzyme telomerase won the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 2009.

examples.hanzi: 这是一场关系到生死的大手术。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì yì chǎng guānxì dào shēngsǐ de dà shǒushù.
examples.english: This is a major operation on which life depends.

examples.hanzi: 他们共同度过了生死难关。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen gòngtóng dùguò le shēngsǐ nánguān.
examples.english: They went through a life-and-death crisis together.

components.note: 艹 (grass, 草字头) — marks plants and herbs, as in 花 flower, 草 grass, 菜 vegetable; 芬 is fragrance from plants, as in 芬芳.
分 (fēn) — same sound: 芬 fēn. 分 also sounds out 纷 fēn and 氛 fēn.

example.hanzi: 花园里充满了芬芳。
example.pinyin: Huāyuán lǐ chōngmǎn le fēnfāng.
example.english: The garden is full of fragrance.
example.fact: 芬 means fragrance and forms 芬芳 (fragrant). It is also a typical girl's name, and it supplies the sound in 芬兰 (Finland).

examples.hanzi: 雨后的空气里有花的芬芳。
examples.pinyin: Yǔ hòu de kōngqì lǐ yǒu huā de fēnfāng.
examples.english: After the rain, the air carries the fragrance of flowers.

examples.hanzi: 她叫小芬，是我的邻居。
examples.pinyin: Tā jiào Xiǎofēn, shì wǒ de línjū.
examples.english: Her name is Xiaofen and she is my neighbor.

components.note: 亡 (wáng) is a close sound clue for wàng; it also sounds out 忘 wàng (forget) and 网 wǎng.
月 (moon) — to gaze up at the moon, so to look into the distance, then to hope.

example.hanzi: 他望着窗外的月亮。
example.pinyin: Tā wàng zhe chuāng wài de yuèliang.
example.english: He gazes at the moon outside the window.
example.fact: 望 is to gaze into the distance, and from longing comes hope: 希望, 失望 (disappointed), 看望 (to visit someone). 望子成龙 expresses parents' hope that their son will "become a dragon," meaning succeed.

examples.hanzi: 我们站在山顶远望，风景真美。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zhàn zài shāndǐng yuǎnwàng, fēngjǐng zhēn měi.
examples.english: We stood on the mountaintop looking far away, and the view was lovely.

examples.hanzi: 妈妈很期望我能考上大学。
examples.pinyin: Māma hěn qīwàng wǒ néng kǎoshàng dàxué.
examples.english: Mom really hopes I can get into university.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — a picture of an open mouth; as a radical it appears in characters of speech, eating and sounds — 吃, 喝, 叫, 吗.
禾 (grain) — 香 originally combined grain with 甘 (sweet): the smell of cooked grain, in modern writing 日 stands in for 甘.
米 (rice, grain) — marks grain and food, as in 粉, 粮, 饭; 糖 is sugar, once made from grain.
唐 (táng) gives the sound exactly: 糖 táng, also in 塘 táng.

example.hanzi: 他嚼着口香糖走进教室。
example.pinyin: tā jiáozhe kǒuxiāngtáng zǒujìn jiàoshì.
example.english: He walked into the classroom chewing gum.
example.fact: Modern chewing gum traces back to chicle, a natural latex harvested from the sapodilla tree in Central America, which businessman Thomas Adams tried and failed to turn into a rubber substitute in the 1870s. Unable to make it work as rubber, he added flavoring and sold it as gum instead, launching a global industry almost by accident.

examples.hanzi: 课堂上请不要嚼口香糖。
examples.pinyin: Kètáng shàng qǐng bú yào jiáo kǒuxiāngtáng.
examples.english: Please don't chew gum in class.

examples.hanzi: 我买了一包薄荷口香糖。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ mǎi le yì bāo bòhe kǒuxiāngtáng.
examples.english: I bought a pack of mint chewing gum.

components.note: 人 (person) — one person following another: 从 means to follow, then "from".
刂 (knife) — the right-hand side. Usually about cutting (到, 别, 利), but not in 前: it is a later corruption of the old picture.
舟 (boat) — hidden in the old form: a foot on a boat moving ahead, so 'in front, forward'. Usual explanation, though the modern shape hides it.

example.hanzi: 从前有一个小村庄。
example.pinyin: cóngqián yǒu yī gè xiǎo cūnzhuāng.
example.english: Once upon a time there was a small village.
example.fact: Homer's epic poems, the Iliad and the Odyssey, are believed to have circulated orally for generations, passed down by professional bards who memorized and improvised the verses, before being written down around the 8th century BCE. This oral tradition relied on repeated formulas and rhythmic patterns that made such enormous poems possible to memorize.

examples.hanzi: 从前，他住在一个小镇上。
examples.pinyin: Cóngqián, tā zhù zài yí ge xiǎo zhèn shàng.
examples.english: In the past, he lived in a small town.

examples.hanzi: 她现在比从前更自信了。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiànzài bǐ cóngqián gèng zìxìn le.
examples.english: She is more confident now than before.

components.note: 火 (fire) — a picture of flames, and a component seen in 烧, 灯, 热 (as the dots 灬), 炒; fire radical for burning and heat.
火 (fire) — a burning torch; also in 灯 lamp, 烧 burn.
巨 (jù) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 距 jù, 拒 jù and 矩 jǔ.

example.hanzi: 运动员高举着火炬跑进体育场。
example.pinyin: yùndòngyuán gāojǔzhe huǒjù pǎojìn tǐyùchǎng.
example.english: The athlete ran into the stadium holding the torch high.
example.fact: The modern Olympic torch relay was introduced at the 1936 Berlin Games, and since then the flame has been carried across oceans by ship, flown by plane, and even carried underwater near Australia's Great Barrier Reef during the 2000 Sydney torch relay. The flame itself is still lit using a parabolic mirror to focus sunlight at Olympia, Greece, exactly as the ancient Greeks did.

examples.hanzi: 晚上，他们举着火炬游行。
examples.pinyin: Wǎnshang, tāmen jǔzhe huǒjù yóuxíng.
examples.english: At night, they paraded holding torches.

examples.hanzi: 奥运会的火炬传遍了很多城市。
examples.pinyin: Àoyùnhuì de huǒjù chuán biàn le hěn duō chéngshì.
examples.english: The Olympic torch was passed through many cities.

components.note: 厂 (cliff) — the frame on the left and top, as in 原, 厚, 压. In 厌 it is just the old cliff-like frame of 厭.
犬 (quǎn, dog) — looks like a sound part but quǎn vs yàn is only a loose hint. The old 厭 got its sound from 猒 (yàn).
心 (heart) — feelings: 想, 思, 感, 怕; 恶 is a bad heart, evil.
亚 (yà) is only a loose sound hint for è.

example.hanzi: 她对谎言感到十分厌恶。
example.pinyin: tā duì huǎngyán gǎndào shífēn yànwù.
example.english: She feels great disgust toward lies.
example.fact: Psychologists classify disgust as one of a small set of universal human emotions, recognizable by the same facial expression across virtually every culture studied. Researchers believe it evolved primarily as a defense mechanism to help early humans avoid spoiled food, disease, and other biological contaminants.

examples.hanzi: 我厌恶浪费食物的行为。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yànwù làngfèi shíwù de xíngwéi.
examples.english: I detest the act of wasting food.

examples.hanzi: 他厌恶那份无聊的工作。
examples.pinyin: Tā yànwù nà fèn wúliáo de gōngzuò.
examples.english: He loathed that boring job.

components.note: 艹 (plants) — marks grasses and flowers, as in 草, 茶, 菜; 花 is a flower.
化 (huà) hints at the sound: 花 huā is close, and 化 also gives 华 huá and 货 huò.
木 (tree) — wood, as in 桌 table, 板 board; 样 once meant a tree (acorn) and later "form, pattern".
羊 (yáng, sheep) is a near-exact sound clue for yàng; 羊 also sounds out 洋 yáng and 养 yǎng.

example.hanzi: 这条围巾有很多漂亮的花样。
example.pinyin: zhè tiáo wéijīn yǒu hěn duō piàoliang de huāyàng.
example.english: This scarf has many beautiful patterns.
example.fact: The Fibonacci sequence appears repeatedly in nature's patterns, from the spiral arrangement of seeds in a sunflower head to the scales of a pinecone, because it produces one of the most space-efficient ways to pack growing elements. Botanists call this spiral arrangement phyllotaxis, and it shows up across an enormous range of unrelated plant species.

examples.hanzi: 这家店的蛋糕花样很多。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn de dàngāo huāyàng hěn duō.
examples.english: This shop has many kinds of cakes.

examples.hanzi: 他们玩出了各种新花样。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen wán chū le gèzhǒng xīn huāyàng.
examples.english: They came up with all kinds of new tricks.

components.note: 留 (liú) is a sound clue for 溜 liū, 榴 liú and 瘤 liú; as a word it means to stay or keep.
心 (heart) — mind and feelings, as in 想, 思, 感: 意 is what one has in mind.
音 (yīn, sound) is a loose sound clue for yì; 意 itself gives 忆 yì and 亿 yì.

example.hanzi: 请留意脚下的台阶。
example.pinyin: qǐng liúyì jiǎoxià de táijiē.
example.english: Please pay attention to the step underfoot.
example.fact: Meerkats take turns acting as sentries, standing upright on their hind legs atop a mound while the rest of the group forages, ready to bark an alarm call the instant a predator like a hawk or jackal appears. Different alarm calls signal different types of threats, and other meerkats react instantly based on which specific call they hear.

examples.hanzi: 开车时要留意前后的车辆。
examples.pinyin: Kāichē shí yào liúyì qiánhòu de chēliàng.
examples.english: When driving, pay attention to the vehicles in front and behind.

examples.hanzi: 你有没有留意到他今天很安静？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yǒu méiyǒu liúyì dào tā jīntiān hěn ānjìng?
examples.english: Did you notice that he was very quiet today?

components.note: 豆 — an old stemmed serving dish, later borrowed for beans; in 豆腐 tofu, 土豆 potato.

example.hanzi: 我早上喝豆浆，吃包子。
example.pinyin: Wǒ zǎoshang hē dòujiāng, chī bāozi.
example.english: In the morning I drink soy milk and eat steamed buns.
example.fact: 豆 first pictured a ritual stemmed dish, and the "bean" meaning came later as a borrowing. It gives 豆腐 (tofu), 豆浆 (soy milk), 红豆 (red bean). Beans are counted with 颗 or 粒.

examples.hanzi: 我最爱吃的是红豆面包。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuì ài chī de shì hóngdòu miànbāo.
examples.english: What I love eating most is red bean bread.

examples.hanzi: 她在锅里煮了一些绿豆汤。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài guō lǐ zhǔ le yìxiē lǜdòu tāng.
examples.english: She cooked some mung bean soup in the pot.
